quizName: DMV Practice Test #6 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding next to another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit and then exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the vehicle's blind spot. If a hazard appears, you may have no escape route. Speed up or drop back to get away.

questions.question: Which of these provides the best face protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection.

questions.question: When are riders safest?

options.text: On the side of the road.
In the left side of the lane.

questions.explanation: Safe riders make sure other drivers can see them. Use your headlight, brake light, and signals. Position yourself to be as visible as possible.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when riding near stopped or slow-moving cars?

options.text: Pull over and wait until traffic begins to move.
Ride on the shoulder to get through the area as quickly as possible.
Weave between the cars to get through the area as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or slow cars is dangerous. Car doors may open, or cars may pull into traffic. You will have no room to escape. Never ride on the shoulder because other drivers won't expect you there.

questions.question: How much stopping power does a motorcycle's front brake provide?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It supplies at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard?

options.text: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
Coming to a complete stop before you expect to.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing traction on one or both wheels.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard causes you to lose traction on one or both wheels and crash.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, other drivers' blind spots, and road hazards. It shows other drivers your intentions and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: Which of these is usually rectangular shaped?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular and white with black lettering. They tell drivers the rules of the road. You must follow these signs.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your riding?

options.text: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
There is usually no effect on the body.
There is an effect on the body, but it only lasts for a short time.
There is an effect on the body, but it can be eliminated by drinking coffee.

questions.correctAnswerText: Judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your judgment and riding skills. Only time allows your body to eliminate alcohol. Drinking coffee does not help.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle at night compared to daytime, which of the following should you NOT do?

options.text: Keep more space between your motorcycle and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: To avoid a crash at night, ride slower and stay farther behind other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road better. Change your lane position when needed, especially at night.

questions.question: During your pre-ride inspection, which of the following should you NOT check?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil, fluids, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Relax your grip on the handlebars.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire fails, grip the handlebars firmly and slow down by easing off the throttle. Go straight. If you must brake, slowly apply the brake on the good tire. Move toward the side of the road as you slow down, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: When you are about to pass another vehicle on the left, where should you ride in your lane?

options.text: In the right portion of the lane.
In the left portion of the lane.
As close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Without signaling, so you don't distract the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when passing. Signal your intention and check for traffic. Pass only when it is safe. Then signal again and return to your original lane.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Your face less well than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face and eyes. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield does not give adequate protection.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the leftmost portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and go straight at a steady speed. Zigzagging to stop the weave will make it more dangerous.

questions.question: Which of the following protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: In a crash, you have a better chance of avoiding serious injury if you do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Reduce your risk of injury by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: During acceleration, what happens to a sidecar attached to a motorcycle?

options.text: It feels like it is lagging behind.
It feels like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: It feels like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. Because of inertia, it will feel like it is lagging behind when you speed up.

questions.question: When securing a load on your motorcycle, where should you place it?

options.text: Only on one side of the motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Loads should be placed low. High loads, like on a sissy bar, raise the center of gravity and throw off balance. Distribute loads evenly on both sides of the motorcycle.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you if they look at you.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection quickly.
Speed up so others will notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcyclists but fail to notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: What can you do to reduce your chances of crashing?

options.text: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
Only look 15 feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Don't use your headlight during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make yourself visible, signal your intentions, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead at least 12 seconds, spot hazards, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: How does carrying a passenger or cargo affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It takes less time to speed up, but more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up and more time to stop.
It takes more time to speed up, but less time to stop.
It takes less time to speed up and less time to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes more time to speed up and more time to stop.
questions.explanation: Extra weight from a passenger or cargo makes your motorcycle slower to speed up and slower to stop compared to riding alone.

questions.question: Where is the gearshift lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: In front of the left footrest
In front of the right footrest

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is located in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. The safest approach is to assume that any vehicle that could enter your path will do so.
